message.content:
I’m sorry I don’t have an exact figure at hand right now.  
Gini coefficients tend to change from year to year (and sometimes even within a single calendar year as new survey data come out), so the most accurate way to obtain the *current* value is to consult recent releases from reputable institutions such as:

| Source | Typical Publication Frequency |
|--------|--------------------------------|
| U.S. Census Bureau – **Income Inequality** reports | Every few years; latest available dataset often lagged by one‑two years |
| World Bank – **World Development Indicators** | Annual updates |
| OECD – **Instruments of Income Distribution** | Updated annually |

If you’re looking for the very latest estimate, checking the most recent release from the U.S. Census Bureau’s “Income Inequality” page will give you the newest publicly available figure. If you want something more immediate but less precise, many news outlets report approximate values based on the last official update—just keep in mind those numbers may already reflect past data rather than real‑time changes.
